skill.name: dast-zap
skill.description: Dynamic application security testing guidance for OWASP ZAP. The skill provides scan workflows, CI templates, authentication guidance, API testing patterns, and reporting advice for authorized web application assessments.
skill.summary: Run authorized OWASP ZAP DAST workflows for web applications and APIs.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are documentation or template examples for authorized OWASP ZAP DAST workflows, so they were dismissed as false positives. Confirmed issues remain for a privileged CI package-install step, an unsafe API-key-in-URL example, and hardcoded sample credentials in reusable authentication templates.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded sample passwords appear in authentication templates and examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace literal passwords with environment-variable placeholders and add comments that real credentials must never be committed.

remediation.issue: The API testing guide shows an API key in a query string.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the query-string API key pattern and recommend headers or environment-backed secret injection instead.

remediation.issue: The GitHub Actions template installs jq with sudo during the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned container image or preinstalled runner tooling to avoid runtime privileged package installation.

static_findings.snippet: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq
Consult `references/api_testing_guide.md` for advanced API testing patterns including authentication
Map findings to OWASP Top 10 using `references/owasp_mapping.md`.
See `scripts/ci_integration.sh` for complete CI/CD integration examples.
- `zap_baseline_scan.sh` - Automated baseline scanning with configurable targets and reporting
- `zap_full_scan.sh` - Comprehensive active scanning with exclusion rules
- `zap_api_scan.py` - API testing with OpenAPI/GraphQL specification support
- `zap_auth_scanner.py` - Authenticated scanning with multiple authentication methods
- `ci_integration.sh` - CI/CD integration examples for Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions
- `authentication_guide.md` - Complete authentication configuration for form-based, OAuth, and token
- `owasp_mapping.md` - Mapping of ZAP alerts to OWASP Top 10 2021 and CWE classifications
- `api_testing_guide.md` - Advanced API testing patterns for REST, GraphQL, SOAP, and WebSocket
- `scan_policies.md` - Custom scan policy configuration for different application types
- `false_positive_handling.md` - Common false positives and verification techniques
- `zap_context.xml` - Context configuration with authentication and session management
- `scan_policy_modern_web.policy` - Scan policy optimized for modern JavaScript applications
- `scan_policy_api.policy` - Scan policy for REST and GraphQL APIs
docker run -t zaproxy/zap-stable zap-baseline.py -t https://target-app.com -r baseline-report.html
docker run -t zaproxy/zap-stable zap-full-scan.py -t https://target-app.com -r full-scan-report.html
docker run --network zap-network -t zaproxy/zap-stable zap-baseline.py -t http://app-container:8080
- **Rate Limiting**: Configure scan speed to avoid overwhelming target applications or triggering DD
# Format: alert_id  URL_pattern  parameter  CWE_id  WARN|IGNORE|FAIL

content.value_statement: Security teams need repeatable runtime testing before releases. This skill guides authorized OWASP ZAP scans, authentication setup, API testing, and CI reporting.
actual_capabilities: Explains baseline, full, API, and authenticated OWASP ZAP scan workflows.
Provides GitHub Actions and GitLab CI templates for ZAP scan automation.
Includes ZAP automation and authentication context templates for customization.
Maps common ZAP alerts to OWASP Top 10 and CWE categories.
Gives guidance for validating and suppressing ZAP false positives.
limitations: Requires Docker and OWASP ZAP access in the user environment.
Active scanning must only run against systems with explicit authorization.
Some helper scripts and scan policy files referenced by the guide are not included.
Scan results still need human validation before remediation decisions.

use_cases.title: Add DAST to release checks
use_cases.description: Create a CI job that runs ZAP against staging and publishes reports for release review.

use_cases.title: Test authenticated application areas
use_cases.description: Configure ZAP authentication context files and test protected pages with dedicated test accounts.

use_cases.title: Validate API security coverage
use_cases.description: Use OpenAPI, GraphQL, or SOAP guidance to scan API endpoints and review findings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a baseline scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a staging web application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an authorized OWASP ZAP baseline scan for my staging URL. Include scope, report outputs, and safe defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Create CI scan steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate automation for a build pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft CI steps for an OWASP ZAP scan against staging. Include artifacts, thresholds, and how to handle scan failures.

prompt_templates.title: Configure authenticated scanning
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing for protected application areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through an authenticated ZAP scan using test credentials from environment variables and a verification URL.

prompt_templates.title: Review API DAST strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an OWASP ZAP API testing workflow for OpenAPI and GraphQL endpoints. Include authentication, rate limits, and reporting.

output_examples.input: Plan a ZAP scan for a staging application before release.
output: Recommended a baseline scan on every merge request and a full scan before release.
Defined staging scope, report artifacts, and thresholds for high and medium findings.
Added authorization, rate limiting, and report review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Set up authenticated scanning for a form login.
output: Outlined required login URL, test account, password environment variable, and verification URL.
Explained session checks and re-authentication handling for long scans.
Included guidance to keep credentials out of repository files.

output_examples.input: Triage ZAP findings after a scan.
output: Grouped findings by severity and OWASP category.
Separated likely false positives from items needing manual verification.
Suggested next remediation steps and evidence to collect.

best_practices: Use dedicated staging targets and written authorization for every active scan.
Store scan credentials in environment variables or a secrets manager.
Review high-risk findings manually before suppressing or closing them.
anti_patterns: Run active scans against production or third-party systems without approval.
Commit ZAP context files that contain real passwords or API tokens.
Suppress all ZAP findings without documented verification.

faq.question: Does this skill run OWASP ZAP by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates that a user or agent can apply in an authorized environment.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains form, token, OAuth, and basic authentication patterns for ZAP scans.

faq.question: Can it scan APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers OpenAPI, GraphQL, SOAP, and manual API testing approaches.

faq.question: Is active scanning safe for production?
faq.answer: Active scanning can send attack payloads. Use staging or maintenance windows unless production approval is explicit.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. ZAP findings need validation, context, and prioritization by qualified reviewers.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Docker and OWASP ZAP are the primary requirements. Some workflows may also use Python, Java, or CI tooling.
